briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-001
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- warehouse roof: (43, -136), roof
- office roof: (68, 31), roof
- control room: (-15, 137), indoor
- electrical room: (-49, 101), indoor
- workcell West: (78, 97), indoor
- east fence: (81, 59), outdoor
- water tank: (105, -24), outdoor
- south yard: (-111, -123), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 5 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3180 s, including the return to its start.
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 8 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3540 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 960 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 6 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect warehouse roof with a camera. Location: warehouse roof. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T2: Run a thermal scan of east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 90 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T3: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at south yard and keep it on board. Location: south yard. Duration: 60 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).
- T5: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 270 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T6: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 270 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 720 s.
- T7: Collect a soil sample (1 kg) at east fence and keep it on board. Location: east fence. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 1 kg).
- T8: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at water tank and keep it on board. Location: water tank. Duration: 90 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T9: Tighten the valve at workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 210 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T10: Deliver the battery pack (1 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 1 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Keep at least 1 quadcopter on standby: it must not be given any task.
6. Every task must be finished by t = 1500 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: warehouse roof (43, -136, a rooftop); office roof (68, 31, a rooftop); control room (-15, 137, indoors); electrical room (-49, 101, indoors); workcell West (78, 97, indoors); east fence (81, 59, outside); water tank (105, -24, outside); south yard (-111, -123, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 5 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 53 minutes including getting back. A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 8 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 59 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 7.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 16 minutes including the flight home. D2 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 6 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 23 minutes including the flight home.

Jobs:
(T1) Have a look at warehouse roof - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T2) Do a heat check over east fence - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Have a look at office roof - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T4) Pick up a soil sample at south yard and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T5) Someone has to tighten the valve at workcell West - that takes 4.5 minutes on site.
(T6) The valve at workcell West needs tightening - that takes 4.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 12 minutes.
(T7) Pick up a soil sample at east fence and keep it on board; it weighs 1 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T8) Pick up a soil sample at water tank and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T9) Someone has to tighten the valve at workcell West - that takes 3.5 minutes on site.
(T10) Get the battery pack (1 kg) over to control room - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.

Keep one quadcopter on standby; don't give it any jobs. Everything has to be wrapped up within 25 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
